title: Move The Prius
mood: petty, loud and very pleased with itself
subject: a diss track aimed at the neighbour whose Prius blocks your driveway every Thursday
caption: West Coast ratchet rap in the Mustard style, the Los Angeles club sound. TR-808 claps doubled with finger snaps on two and four; a deep 808 sub holding long notes under the riff; a staccato two-note synth-bass riff that bounces under every bar; sparse straight hi-hats with no rolls; a short loop of synth brass stabs and piano under the hook. Dry and loud with a lot of empty space, the claps and the lead voice forward, nothing washed in reverb. Male rap voice, aggressive and conversational with a grin in it, a gang of men shouting 'hey!' as the answer on the hook lines. 100 BPM, F minor. Petty, loud and very pleased with itself. No trap hi-hat triplet rolls, no sliding trap 808s, no distorted rage synth lead, no sung R&B chorus, no autotune, no dreamy keys.
lyrics:
[Intro - claps, snaps and a two-note synth bass]

[Verse 1]
Thursday morning, seven-oh-two, and I'm late again
Silver Prius parked across my driveway like it pays the rent
Little sunshade on the dash with a cartoon cat
I left a note on the windshield, he drew a smiley on the back
Bumper sticker says "coexist", Ken, coexist with my gate
Now I'm backing out across the lawn through my own tomato bed

[Hook]
Move the Prius! (Hey!)
Move the Prius! (Hey!)
Number forty-one, I know you're home, Ken
Move the Prius! (Hey!) Tell the cat I said it

[Verse 2]
He opens up the door in a robe, holding a mug of tea
Says "oh, is that a driveway?" Ken, it's got a gate, a curb cut and me
Ten years on the same street and we never said a word
Now I made a whole song about you, and I know you heard
I called the city, lady asked me "is it blocking all of it?"
I said half, ma'am, but it's the half my car is parked behind

[Hook]
Move the Prius! (Hey!)
Move the Prius! (Hey!)
Ken is on the porch with his tea and he's nodding
Don't dance to it, Ken! (Hey!) It's about you!

[Outro - claps drop out, sub rings out]
Next Thursday, seven-oh-two
I'm parking on his lawn
